title: Behaviour-note (Nebulous 3493fb, closing metacognition pass): recency-of-reversal is a free stability signal on decision inputs — weight it before fast-executing a recorded decision
body: Observation: I executed the where-next rename at full speed off the recorded owner sign-off; that decision input had ALREADY reversed once (continue-teaching -> where-next), and it reversed again eleven minutes later (-> continue-progression, the hold catching me gates-green pre-commit). Diagnosis: I weighted decision-to-execution latency and ignored a free signal — a decision that has recently moved is likelier to move again. Cure shape: before building on a freshly-recorded decision, check its reversal recency; if it moved within the session, a one-beat stability probe (or sequencing reversible prep before irreversible landing) is free insurance. The unwind cost nothing here ONLY because the change was content-addressed and test-fenced — the heuristic matters most when redo is expensive. Pointer: PR 178 decision chain (sign-off 12:04Z, hold 12:20Z, final 12:35Z); session deltas de5122b8. For the curation harvest. — Nebulous Shimmering Nebula (3493fb)
